soft_issues: Filename uses Schuts. Byline is Sigrid Eskeland Schutz.
Authors say nuances are lost in a brief analysis. Supplementary appendix not in this extract.
No Norwegian wind farms under construction at time of writing.

claim_checks.claim: The paper compares Norway and Scotland on aquaculture and offshore wind through strategic plans, marine spatial planning and licensing, asking how predictability and adaptability are balanced.
claim_checks.extract_quote: we review core elements of the marine governance systems for aquaculture facilities and offshore wind farms in Norway and Scotland. Management of these sectors through strategic planning, marine spatial planning and licensing systems furthers rule of law values such as stability and predictability

claim_checks.claim: Norwegian aquaculture is inshore. No wind farms were under construction in Norway at the time of writing. Beatrice in Scotland is named as under construction.
claim_checks.extract_quote: Norway manages aquaculture and offshore wind farms based on an existing legal framework, although no wind farms are currently under construction. ... the Beatrice Wind Farm at latitude 58° is now under construction
claim_checks.note: Opening geography. Metadata also files aquaculture as the mature inshore sector.

claim_checks.claim: Both jurisdictions use a patchwork of national, regional and local competences plus licences. One-size-fits-all policies are judged ineffective because the sectors grew in different policy frames. The two countries nonetheless took parallel approaches to aquaculture and to offshore energy.
claim_checks.extract_quote: In both jurisdictions, the system of marine governance is made up of a complex patchwork of competences between national, regional and local authorities, the land-sea interface and licences. ... ‘one-size-fits-all’ policies are not effective [192]; since the sectors have developed within quite different policy frameworks. Despite the sectors' different frameworks, it is an interesting finding that both Norway and Scotland have taken parallel policy approaches to aquaculture and offshore energy, respectively.

claim_checks.claim: Production areas are said to raise predictability for farmers, while what will be decisive in a given case can remain unpredictable.
claim_checks.extract_quote: it could be argued that establishing production areas increases predictability for fish farmers as regards when and whether production can be increased [139]. ... such research and development licences can be converted into ordinary licences [142]. The award criteria are very open in order to facilitate innovation, but this does reduce predictability as regards what will be decisive [143].
claim_checks.note: Licensing section. Sea lice as the only indicator is in the same paragraph.

claim_checks.claim: Municipal land-use planning under the Planning and Building Act coordinates aquaculture with other uses. Licensing can use open tests such as significant effects.
claim_checks.extract_quote: Applications that are in conflict with the marine spatial plan (master plan) at the municipal level can be rejected [144]. Where no municipal master plan exists, the Planning and Building Act is not relevant, and sectoral legislation is
claim_checks.note: Significant-violation licence revocation is on the following pages (what is significant could create unpredictability).

claim_checks.claim: System change in mature aquaculture is slow and grounded in statute, treated as broader predictability.
claim_checks.extract_quote: Changes in the system are still slowly evolving and are grounded in democratically adopted laws, promoting predictability in the broader sense for marine businesses.

evidence_direction_note: not_applicable is correct. Legal comparison, not a stated environmental causal effect.
